Inside Hostos Community College's Repertory Theater, hundreds of students, tenants, organizers, educators, and community advocates gathered on May 28 to confront one of the defining questions facing New York City: Can young people still afford to build a future here? The setting could not have been more fitting.

The College's Repertory Theater was packed and buzzing with proud family members clutching babies and bouquets, snapping photos and exclaiming excitedly as their graduates were recognized for their resilience, dedication, and achievements. In all, 22 Licensed Practical Nurses (LPN) and 19 Registered Nurses (RN) were pinned and will soon be entering the job market.

slu.title: SLU Remembers Assemblymember Catherine Nolan, A Champion for Labor and Education
slu.description: Catherine Nolan, a Queens lawmaker who served in the State Assembly for almost four decades and was widely known as a fierce advocate for workers’ rights, passed away on March 11, one day before her 68th birthday.

slu.title: Organizer in the Classroom: Inneshia Hart’s Fight for Workers—and a Degree
slu.description: Having a child alters your life, it’s safe to say. But you won’t know how, exactly, until it occurs.

slu.title: Beyond the Ivory Tower: Q&A With Professor Penny Lewis
slu.description: Professor of Labor Studies Penny Lewis is union through and through. Lewis is one of the original full-time faculty members of the School of Labor and Urban Studies, and worked at its predecessor, the Joseph S. Murphy Institute, beginning in 2009.

slu.title: Calling All Students: Write for Your New Monthly Column
slu.description: Every movement needs stories, and today, I want to tell you mine. I didn’t come to CUNY SLU because I had everything figured out. I came as a new shop steward suddenly guiding members through issues bigger than me. I realized quickly that this work takes skill, knowledge, and support, and I needed all three.

slu.description: Due to the impending blizzard, the SLU campus will operate fully remotely on Monday, February 23, 2026. All classes and administrative operations will be conducted remotely, and all on-campus events are canceled.

slu.title: From Melrose to SLU: Meet Bronx Blogger Ed García Conde
slu.description: You can count on New Yorkers to express a full spectrum of feelings about the many diverse neighborhoods they call home. For Bronx residents, though, there’s something specific and shared about how they relate to their slice of NYC. Something earnest and unpretentious. What is it?

slu.title: Q&A With Asst. Prof. Cameron Black: Making Students Wild About History
slu.description: The first time that Assistant Professor of Labor Studies Cameron Black set foot in New York City was when he moved across the country to join the SLU faculty for the 2023-2024 academic year.

slu.title: Rising Up: SLU Toasts Scholarship Winners
slu.description: One of the most special events of the SLU year occurred on Tuesday, June 9th: the reception and award ceremony for winners of the Joseph S. Murphy Scholarship for Diversity in Labor. Awardees, their families and friends, and SLU faculty and staff mingled and celebrated on the 18th floor.

slu.title: Celebrating the Capstone of the SLU Experience
slu.description: In the spring semester at SLU, “Capstone” is the buzzword! Students work hard on their biggest research projects – but most SLU community members are unaware of what’s being researched.

slu.title: Congratulations to the Class of 2026!
slu.description: A spirited Commencement ceremony for the School of Labor and Urban Studies took place at Town Hall on May 28. Graduates from all Labor Studies and Urban Studies programs strolled — and in a few cases, danced and strutted – across the stage to accept their certificates and bachelor’s or master’s degrees from Founding Dean Greg Mantsios.

slu.title: Finding My Voice: Growth and Purpose at SLU
slu.description: This semester has been a powerful chapter in my journey as a student, union member, and emerging leader. At CUNY SLU, I’ve made meaningful progress toward my Bachelor of Labor Studies major, and I recently learned that I only have 14 credits left before I graduate. This realization has been incredibly motivating and reminds me of how far I’ve come.
